title: Payment API latency spike
executive_summary: Payment API latency and 5xx errors (INC-001) are caused by exhaustion of payment-service's DB connection pool (payment-db-pool). Connections leaked on the RefundService.processPartialRefund path were held for more than 30s starting about 13:45Z. Pool utilization climbed from about 13:49Z and reached 100% by 14:25Z. From 14:00Z, requests waited on the pool, timed out after 5s, and surfaced as p95 latency of about 2.7-3s and error rates near 20%. API gateway latency and errors follow the payment-service degradation. Auth, Postgres latency, CPU and disk are not implicated. No deployment or config change to payment-service was found in the window; the leak's trigger is unconfirmed.

hypotheses.description: Connection leak in the refund path (RefundService.processPartialRefund) exhausted payment-db-pool, causing acquisition timeouts, latency and 5xx. Mechanism: Refund code paths acquire DB connections and do not release them. Leak detection fires from 13:45Z with connections held >30s. Active connections reach the pool max of 50 with 0 idle, so new requests wait and time out after 5000ms. Latency and timeouts follow, which propagates to api-gateway.

probable_root_cause.description: Connection leak in the refund path (RefundService.processPartialRefund) exhausted payment-db-pool, causing acquisition timeouts, latency and 5xx.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): db_connection_pool_exhaustion in payment-service - Connection leak in the refund path (RefundService.processPartialRefund) exhausted payment-db-pool, causing acquisition timeouts, latency and 5xx.
corrective_actions: Restart payment-service pods to release leaked connections and restore capacity (short-term mitigation).
Fix the leaked connection in RefundService.processPartialRefund by using try-with-resources or a finally-block release, then deploy.
Add a statement or transaction timeout so refund connections cannot be held indefinitely.
preventive_actions: Alert on Hikari leak-detection warnings and on pool utilization above 80% for more than 5 minutes.
Add a load and soak test covering partial refund flows that checks for connection returns.
monitoring_recommendations: Track payment-db-pool active, idle and waiting counts per pod.
Track count of 'Connection leak detection triggered' logs by call site.
Watch payment-service timeout_rate and p95 latency with recovery after the pod restart.
limitations: Historical match similarity is low (0.275) and serves as an analogy only.
Config and deployment queries returned no payment-service changes, which limits trigger analysis.
[agent-reported gap] No refund traffic or code-change data in the window.
[agent-reported gap] No thread dump or pool connection-owner snapshot.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely root cause is a connection leak in the refund path (RefundService.processPartialRefund) that exhausted payment-service's DB connection pool beginning about 13:45Z. This caused acquisition timeouts from 14:00Z, which produced the latency and 5xx symptoms seen by api-gateway and customers. Auth, Postgres and payment CPU are ruled out as primary causes. Confidence is high but the leak trigger is not confirmed, so the status is PROBABLE_ROOT_CAUSE.
